title: gRPC vs WebSocket vs Webhook
sources: Stripe Docs, 'Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint' docs.stripe.com/webhooks (Stripe pushes events as HTTPS requests to your endpoint; endpoints must be publicly accessible HTTPS URLs; verify the Stripe-Signature header; return 2xx quickly; automatic retries for up to three days in live mode; the same event may arrive more than once, so log processed event IDs)
MDN Web Docs, 'WebSockets API' (a two-way interactive communication session between the user's browser and a server; send messages and receive responses without having to poll)

gRPC docs, 'Introduction to gRPC' grpc.io/docs/what-is-grpc/introduction (Protocol Buffers by default) and 'Core concepts' (bidirectional streaming RPCs: both sides send a sequence of messages using a read-write stream)
gRPC repository, 'gRPC over HTTP2' github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md (gRPC carried over HTTP/2 framing)
grpc-web repository, github.com/grpc/grpc-web (gRPC-web clients connect to gRPC services via a special proxy; Envoy by default)
Typical, not measured: 'every open connection costs the server memory' is a general rule of thumb; no benchmark is claimed. Payment example and field names are illustrative.

lines.text: A payment just succeeded, so does your server keep asking, or wait to be told?
lines.caps: A PAYMENT *SUCCEEDED | KEEP *ASKING? | OR WAIT TO BE *TOLD?

lines.text: Being told is a webhook: the other service sends an HTTP request to your URL.
lines.caps: BEING TOLD IS A *WEBHOOK | AN HTTP *REQUEST | TO YOUR *URL

lines.text: It's one way, so your server must be reachable, and it should verify the signature.
lines.caps: IT'S *ONE WAY | MUST BE *REACHABLE | VERIFY THE *SIGNATURE

lines.text: A WebSocket keeps one connection open, so either side can send a message any time.
lines.caps: A *WEBSOCKET | ONE CONNECTION *OPEN | EITHER SIDE *ANY TIME

lines.text: That's why chat and live prices use it, though each open connection costs memory.
lines.caps: *CHAT AND LIVE PRICES | EACH CONNECTION COSTS *MEMORY

lines.text: And gRPC lets one service call another's functions, with typed binary messages over HTTP two.
But here's the catch: browsers need a proxy layer, called gRPC web, to reach gRPC services.
lines.caps: BUT HERE'S THE *CATCH | BROWSERS NEED A *PROXY | CALLED GRPC *WEB

lines.text: And a webhook can arrive twice or fail, so plan for retries and duplicates.
lines.caps: A WEBHOOK CAN *ARRIVE TWICE | OR *FAIL | PLAN FOR *DUPLICATES

lines.text: Pick by who's talking: server to you, webhook; browser live, WebSocket; service to service, gRPC.
lines.caps: PICK BY WHO'S *TALKING | SERVER TO YOU: *WEBHOOK | BROWSER LIVE: *WEBSOCKET | SERVICE TO SERVICE: *GRPC
